name: Papillon (French Fishing)
description: Papillon (Butterfly) is a classic French fishing-type card game, conceptually similar to Scopa but with its own distinct bonus system and 'Talon' (stock) mechanics. Players use cards from their hand to capture cards from the table, either by matching ranks or sums. It is beloved for its evocative bonus names ('Grasshopper', 'Little Beetle') and its emphasis on being the first to 'fly away' by emptying one's hand. It is primarily a game of observation and tactical capturing.

content.text: Papillon (Butterfly) is a classic French fishing-type card game, conceptually similar to Scopa but with its own distinct bonus system and 'Talon' (stock) mechanics. Players use cards from their hand to capture cards from the table, either by matching ranks or sums. It is beloved for its evocative bonus names ('Grasshopper', 'Little Beetle') and its emphasis on being the first to 'fly away' by emptying one's hand. It is primarily a game of observation and tactical capturing.
Dates back to the 18th century as a social salon game in France. It shares DNA with Italian fishing games like Scopa and the Middle Eastern game of Basra.
52 cards. Each player receives 3 cards initially; 7 more face-up to the tableau (3 players) or 4 (4 players); remainder as talon. After each round when hands are empty, deal 3 more each from talon.
Deal 3 cards each to hand (first hand to dealer's left), then 7 face-up to the tableau (4 in four-hand). Stack the remainder face down as talon. When all hands are empty, deal 3 more each from talon.

items.text: Four-hand Papillon: Four players; dealer lays only 4 upcards on the tableau instead of 7. Otherwise the same as three-player.

Modern rules: Simplified scoring: each player antes 1 or 2 jetons to the pot; each card trailed (except Aces) pays 1 jeton to the pot; each Ace trailed is paid 1 jeton by each opponent to the player; Papillon wins and sweeps the pot, or most cards wins if no-one achieves Papillon.
